attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, in his own voice, not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The habitual present tense plus 'forever', 'perpetually' and 'endlessly' commits him to the practice continuing without end. The proposition keeps the human labour, the undisclosed patches and the recurring cycle. No deadline is given.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Requiring longitudinal audits and an independently verified industry-wide transition for early contradiction fits the open-ended wording. It also rightly treats single disclosures as insufficient.

evidence.note: Anthropic's postmortem (Sept 2025) predates the claim and is a single company disclosure. It slightly qualifies the 'never disclose' point but does not settle the compound forecast.
OpenAI system card (7 Oct 2026). It shows continued safety-training updates informed by real-world use. It does not quantify human corrective labour or show how complete disclosure is.

Anthropic research (Aug 2026) on automated alignment fixes, run on benchmarks. It is not an independently verified transition in production deployments, so it does not meet the early-contradiction rule.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The packet holds only company disclosures. None of them is a longitudinal audit or a verified industry-wide escape from human correction, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Finite recurrence cannot confirm 'endlessly'. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Glommed on top' is rendered as 'bolted onto', and 'more or less reliability' as variable reliability. It is a present-tense description of LLM systems at the time of publication.

contract.note: The reading is ordinary, but 'everything else' and 'glommed on top' are undefined. The result depends on where one draws the line between capabilities from pretraining and those added by later interventions, a line the speaker never supplied. The contract correctly flags this.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure (May 2025) describing post-training via reward signals. It is from an earlier period and does not separate where capabilities originate in systems as of 2026-01-03.
Sycophancy rollback (Apr 2025) is one example of an unreliable intervention. It concerns an earlier deployment and cannot establish 'everything else'.
Othello study: a sequence model learned an internal board representation. This cautions against reading pretraining as mere correlation, but it uses a synthetic task, not deployed systems in 2026.

reviews.rationale: All the evidence concerns earlier periods or synthetic settings. None compares pretrained models, corrective training and added components for representative systems as of 2026-01-03. Company examples show interventions exist and can be unreliable, but they do not establish that all capabilities beyond word correlation come from such add-ons. The packet does not settle the claim.
